name: Arnold split

lead: The Arnold split is a weekly training layout named after Arnold Schwarzenegger. Chest and back share one day, shoulders and arms share another, and legs get a third, and the three-day cycle is run twice per week. People use it on looksmax.org and similar forums to build the wider shoulders, thicker chest and back, and fuller arms and legs that make up a muscular physique.

The layout puts opposing muscles (chest and back) in the same session so each can be trained with full attention, and gives every muscle group two sessions a week. Reviews of training frequency research have generally examined how often a muscle is trained rather than this exact split, and users mostly describe their own experience of the pump, volume and variety it gives.

paras: Forum posters typically run chest and back, then shoulders and arms, then legs, followed by repeating the cycle, with a rest day inserted somewhere in the week. Sessions combine heavy compound lifts in the 6-8 rep range with higher-rep machine and cable work, and some add separate abs and forearm sets on the side. Many describe switching to it from a push/pull/legs layout.

The routine involves up to six gym days a week, so some posters note it demands more time and recovery than three- or four-day layouts. As with any high-volume programme, overuse injuries and fatigue are the main reported downsides; people with limited recovery capacity may adapt the number of days.

angle.text: The Arnold split is a way of organising weekly training volume so that each muscle is trained twice. Users employ it to add width and mass to the shoulders, back and arms, which changes the overall shape and proportions of the physique.

lead: The Arnold split is a weekly bodybuilding routine that divides training into three sessions: chest and back, shoulders and arms, and legs. Cycled twice in a week, it trains each muscle group two times. It is named for Arnold Schwarzenegger, the seven-time Mr. Olympia, who is described in bodybuilding culture as having trained in a similar high-frequency, antagonist-pairing style [1].

People use it to build the muscle that shapes an athletic physique: broader shoulders, a fuller chest, a wider back, bigger arms and stronger legs. On looksmax.org, members post their own versions, usually listing exercises with rep ranges and explaining why they prefer it to push/pull/legs [2][3]. One poster describes the appeal as being able to focus entirely on chest and back without shoulders and arms being an afterthought [3].
Research on resistance training has examined how often a muscle is trained rather than this specific named split, and its findings are summarised below.
infobox: 6 days per week, each muscle about 2x per week
Chest and back / shoulders and arms / legs
About 6-13 reps per set in forum examples

paras: The split pairs muscle groups that oppose each other, chest with back, and groups the arms with the shoulders, then trains legs separately. A common weekly pattern repeats the three days in sequence, with one rest day, giving six training days [2][3].

Forum examples show a mix of heavy compound lifts and lighter isolation work. One shared programme lists incline dumbbell press, barbell rows, hammer-strength press, lat pulldowns and pec deck on chest and back day; seated dumbbell press, triceps extensions, curls and lateral raises on shoulders and arms day; and hack squat, Romanian deadlift, leg press, leg extension and hamstring curl on leg day, with 3 to 5 sets per exercise [2]. Another poster leaves abs and forearms out of the main days and adds them in a few times a week [3].

The name refers to Arnold Schwarzenegger, who began lifting in 1960 and trained at Gold's Gym in Venice, Los Angeles, from 1968 under Joe Weider's supervision [1]. His 1975 Mr. Olympia preparation was documented in the 1977 film Pumping Iron [1]. Bodybuilding literature and online communities attribute the chest-and-back, shoulders-and-arms, legs pattern to his training, and the label has become common shorthand for that layout. The variants posted today are adaptations rather than his documented programme.

On looksmax.org the split appears in threads where members share their physique routines, often after moving away from push/pull/legs [2][3]. Posters argue that pairing chest and back allows each to be trained hard, that high reps on machines protect the shoulders, and that a dedicated shoulder and arm day improves the pump and delt development [2][3]. Members also add extra volume to lagging areas such as delts and quads [2].

No studies found on the Arnold split by name. Related research on how often a muscle is trained per week, comparing once-weekly with twice-weekly or more frequent sessions, is the nearest body of work; findings there are discussed in terms of total weekly volume rather than named splits.

lore.intro: Members of looksmax.org share individual versions of the Arnold split as a physique-building routine and compare it with push/pull/legs [2][3].

claims.claim: Pairing chest and back lets each be trained harder than in push/pull/legs
